author: nerln
body:
Independent reproduction, before and after, same numbers: a "before" binary built off upstream main (76370e1a6; `vc_render_tifxyz.cpp` is byte-identical to this branch's base 4b3c72882) and an "after" binary built off this branch (ec0eae6f4), both on macOS arm64, same segment, volume, flags and a `--volume` staging directory that did not exist.

Setup: an existing PHerc0125 tifxyz surface and the published PHerc0125 volume zarr on S3, rendered with `--group-idx 1 --scale 2 --num-slices 3 --slice-step 1 --cache-gb 2 --pyramid 0`.

Before, render 1 with `--remote-url <url>`: exit 0, 8 s, 3 tif written (1,910,220 / 1,925,266 / 1,943,606 B; sha256 ceaa3b8b…, a52ffb91…, 64d365de…). The `--volume` directory was never created, matching "the first render works but never creates <dir>" in the description. Render 2, same `--volume`, no `--remote-url`: exit 1, stderr in full: `Error opening local zarr: filesystem error: in directory_iterator::directory_iterator(...): No such file or directory ["<staging>"]`. No `.remote_source.json` anywhere, since main never writes it.

After, render 1 with `--remote-url <url>`: exit 0, 10 s, the same 3 tif byte-for-byte (same three sha256), and one new stdout line right after `Remote zarr streaming: <url>`: `Recorded remote source in <staging>/.remote_source.json`. The directory now exists and holds only that file, `{"url": "<url>"}`. Render 2, same `--volume`, no `--remote-url`: exit 0, 9 s, stdout opens with `Detected cached remote source: <url>`, and the same 3 tif again, identical sha256. The fix does what it claims: the first streamed render records the URL, and a later run against the same `--volume` picks it up instead of failing.

On whether the branch creates `--volume` when it does not exist: yes. `saveRemoteSourceMarker()` calls `std::filesystem::create_directories(volumePath)` before writing the marker, so nothing has to be created by hand.

Two notes from the diff, not from running anything, and not asking to expand the PR: the marker is skipped whenever the URL contains a `?`, which the plain S3 URL here does not, so that path is untested; and the skip when `--volume` already holds a local zarr (`.zgroup`/`.zarray`/`zarr.json`/`0`) is untested too, since only the never-existed directory was tried.

author: CVasilopoulos
body:
Thanks @nerln for the independent before/after on a real PHerc0125 render, including the never-existed `--volume` case.

On the two notes, both are deliberate rather than gaps:

- URLs containing `?` are skipped on purpose: a query string is where presigned S3 URLs and access tokens live, and `.remote_source.json` is a plain-text file that sits next to the cache, so the marker only ever records credential-free URLs. A signed URL still streams exactly as before; it just is not remembered.
- The skip when `--volume` already holds a local zarr (`.zgroup`, `.zarray`, `zarr.json` or `0`) is the guard against turning a real local volume into a "remote" one by accident; it prints `Warning: <dir> holds a local zarr; not recording the remote source` and renders normally.

Neither path changes any output, so I left them out of the PR's own run rather than expanding its scope; happy to add a unit test for both if the maintainers want it.

AI-assisted (Claude Code), human-directed.

author: hendrikschilling
body:
Remote rendering should either take a remote path (and cache in the global vc3d cache) or a local volume -v
I see no good reason to add this mixture?
Cleaning up the interface could involve -v taking urls instead of local paths or making remote-url and -v mutually exclusive.
Reopen with reasoning if you disagree.
